chunks: Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah, from a number of our companions, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no amputation upon the one who snatches, and there is no amputation upon the one who stealthily takes dirhams from a man’s garment.

key_terms.قَطْعٌ: the fixed punishment of amputation for qualifying theft

ai.seo_question: When does the hadd of amputation not apply in cases of theft according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply to one who snatches property openly, nor to one who secretly takes dirhams from a person’s garment in the manner described here. It distinguishes these acts from the form of theft that legally entails the fixed hadd punishment.
